what_we_do: Create one GCP project that holds staging for every app. Production stays in each app's existing project.
tech_stack: GCP project. Placeholder id opptra-staging.
example: gcc-dashboard staging runs in opptra-staging. Its production stays in the warehouse project named in service.yaml.
rules_and_restrictions: Do not create a new user-wise project for an app. Do not fold every production project into one.
verifiers: The project id is the default staging_project input on the deploy and plan workflows. A human checks the project exists before the first app is bound.
agent_instructions: Agents do not create GCP projects.
automation: None. docs/gcp-bootstrap.md is the runbook.
v1_status: Written. Project is not created yet.
discussion_point: Confirm the real project id. opptra-staging is a placeholder. One shared staging project means one app can affect another's staging quota.

step: Bootstrap identity, state, and the image registry
what_we_do: Enable APIs. Create the GitHub Workload Identity pool in the staging project. Create a versioned state bucket named <project>-tfstate in staging and in each prod project. Create the Artifact Registry repo apps in asia-south1.
tech_stack: Workload Identity Federation. Cloud Storage. Artifact Registry. gcloud, run once.
example: gs://opptra-staging-tfstate holds Terraform state. App gcc-dashboard uses the prefix gcc-dashboard.
rules_and_restrictions: No service-account JSON keys in GitHub. Terraform cannot create the state bucket it stores state in, so this step stays manual. Budgets at 50, 90, and 100 percent on the staging project and on each prod project.
verifiers: scripts/bind-repo.sh refuses to run if the state bucket or the Workload Identity pool is missing.
agent_instructions: Agents do not invent a second registry or a second identity pool.
automation: docs/gcp-bootstrap.md. bind-repo.sh creates the apps repo if it is missing when an app is bound.
v1_status: Written. Not executed.
discussion_point: Who runs this once, and who owns the billing alerts?

what_we_do: Create <app>-deployer in the staging project and in the prod project. Let only that GitHub repo impersonate it. Grant it permission to apply Terraform and push images.
tech_stack: scripts/bind-repo.sh. GitHub Actions variables WIF_PROVIDER_* and WIF_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_*.
example: opptra/finance-ops gets finance-ops-deployer@opptra-staging and finance-ops-deployer@<prod project>.
rules_and_restrictions: Humans do not get deploy roles. This script does not create the Cloud Run service or the runtime service account. Those come from Terraform on the first apply.
verifiers: The plan and deploy workflows fail if the Actions variables are empty.
agent_instructions: Do not add a JSON key or a laptop gcloud login as a substitute.
automation: scripts/bind-repo.sh prints the gh variable set commands.
v1_status: Script is in the repo. It has not been run.
discussion_point: The deployer can administer Cloud Run in the whole project, not only this app. Is that acceptable in the shared staging project?

what_we_do: Open a Linear issue before code. It names the users, what the tool does, the production GCP project, and how people sign in: app-login, iap, or public.
tech_stack: Linear. Openspec is optional and stays a file in the repo if a team wants it.
example: Issue: GCC inventory for sales ops, prod project opptra-datawarehouse, auth app-login.
rules_and_restrictions: No production code without an issue. Auth is chosen per app and recorded in service.yaml. The platform does not force one login.
verifiers: The pull request template asks for the Linear link. A reviewer sends the PR back if the link is missing. v1 does not call Linear from CI.
agent_instructions: Read the Linear issue before adding features. Do not invent a second auth mechanism.
automation: None in v1.
v1_status: Process only. Template asks for the link.
discussion_point: Is a Linear link enough, or do we want Openspec required for new apps?

what_we_do: Pick how the app runs. New internal tools use cloud-run-service: one repo, one image, FastAPI serving the Vite build.
tech_stack: service.yaml field archetype. Values: cloud-run-service, cloud-run-job, vm-worker, apps-script, config-only.
example: A dashboard is cloud-run-service. A scraper worker is vm-worker. A recipe repo is config-only.
rules_and_restrictions: UI and API go on Cloud Run. A VM is only a worker that cannot run as a request. Postgres goes on Cloud SQL, not on the VM. No Vercel for new work.
verifiers: scripts/check_manifest.py rejects an unknown archetype. The deploy workflow refuses anything other than cloud-run-service.
agent_instructions: rules/cursor/opptra-sdlc.mdc. Do not add Next.js, a second server, or a new language for a new app.
automation: check_manifest.py. The other archetypes have a written rule and no workflow yet.
v1_status: cloud-run-service is in the template. The other four are rules only.
discussion_point: Which existing apps are allowed to stay on a VM, and which must move to Cloud Run?

step: Copy the template and fill service.yaml
what_we_do: Copy template/ into a new opptra repository. Set name, archetype, prod_project, region, and auth. Point infra/main.tf at the shared module.
tech_stack: Python 3.12, uv, Ruff, pytest, FastAPI. Vite, React, TypeScript. Terraform module modules/cloud-run-service. Region asia-south1.
example: name: gcc-dashboard. prod_project: opptra-datawarehouse. region: asia-south1. auth: app-login.
rules_and_restrictions: service.yaml is flat key: value and must match service.schema.json. An old app keeps its language but still adds service.yaml, the workflows, and the agent rules.
verifiers: check_manifest.py. CI on opptra/sdlc validates the template Terraform. CODEOWNERS covers service.yaml.
agent_instructions: AGENTS.md tells the agent to read service.yaml and not invent deploy settings.
automation: docs/new-app.md. No cookiecutter command in v1. Copy is manual.
v1_status: Template is in the repo and its tests passed locally.
discussion_point: Is asia-south1 the region for every new app, including ones whose prod project is elsewhere?

what_we_do: Push main and a staging branch created from it. After the first checks have run, protect both branches.
tech_stack: GitHub branch protection. scripts/protect-branches.sh.
example: Direct push to opptra/finance-ops main is rejected. A pull request is required.
rules_and_restrictions: One approving review. Admins are included. Stale reviews are dismissed. Required checks are ci / ci and plan / plan. No force-push. No deleting the branch.
verifiers: GitHub rejects the push. The script is the way the rule is applied.
agent_instructions: Branch off staging. Do not commit directly to staging or main.
automation: scripts/protect-branches.sh opptra/<repo>.
v1_status: Script is in the repo. It is not applied to any app yet.
discussion_point: Replace @opptra/platform in CODEOWNERS before turning on code-owner review, or the team name will block merges.

what_we_do: Branch off staging. Run the API and the UI locally. Open a pull request back into staging.
tech_stack: git. uv run uvicorn on port 8000. Vite dev server proxies /api to that port.
example: Branch add-inventory-filter off staging. PR targets staging, not main.
rules_and_restrictions: Production is never a direct pull request from a feature branch. Code reaches main only from staging.
verifiers: Branch protection. The plan workflow treats a PR into main as a production plan, so a feature PR aimed at main would plan prod and should be closed.
agent_instructions: AGENTS.md and rules/cursor/opptra-sdlc.mdc. One change per pull request.
automation: None for branch creation.
v1_status: Rule is in the agent files and the docs.
discussion_point: Do we squash-merge into staging? The applied image tag is the commit that lands on the branch, which may differ from the plan shown on the PR.

step: Keep the agent on the stack
what_we_do: Cursor reads vendored AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules. The source copy lives in opptra/sdlc under rules/.
tech_stack: Cursor rules: opptra-sdlc.mdc (always on), python.mdc, react.mdc. Dobby reads dobby/review-brief.md later.
example: The agent is asked for a new page. It adds a Vite route and a FastAPI route under /api. It does not add Next.js.
rules_and_restrictions: New UI is Vite, React, and TypeScript. New API is FastAPI. Routes stay under /api. Product analytics goes only through frontend/src/analytics.ts, which is a no-op. Do not add a deploy.sh. Do not run gcloud run deploy. Do not commit a secret or bake one into an image. Image tag is the git SHA.
verifiers: CI runs Ruff, ESLint, and tsc, which catch style and type breaks. They do not catch a new framework. Dobby is asked to flag a laptop deploy script and a floating image tag. A human still has to notice a new framework in review.
agent_instructions: The three rule files above, copied into the app. Source of truth is opptra/sdlc/rules.
automation: No sync job yet. Each app copies the rules. A later job can fail CI if the copy drifts.
v1_status: Rules are in the repo and in the template.
discussion_point: How often do apps re-copy rules from opptra/sdlc, and who notices when they are stale?

step: Keep secrets out of the repo
what_we_do: Runtime secrets live in Secret Manager in the target project. Staging reads staging secrets. The image build does not contain them.
tech_stack: Secret Manager. Not wired into the Terraform module yet.
example: A finance app's Uniware token is a secret in the prod project. The staging service does not reference an id ending in _PROD.
rules_and_restrictions: No .env committed. No secret in the Docker image. Staging must not use a production secret name.
verifiers: Dobby brief marks a secret in the diff as blocking. There is no secret scanner in CI yet.
agent_instructions: opptra-sdlc.mdc forbids committing secrets. dobby/review-brief.md lists this as blocking.
automation: None for secret scanning in v1. Terraform does not create secret values.
v1_status: Rule and Dobby spec only. The module does not mount secrets yet.
discussion_point: Do we add a secret scanner as a required check before the pilot, given github-mcp-server and catalog-service already leaked credentials?

what_we_do: Use the pull request template. Link the Linear issue. Say whether the diff touches workflows, infra, service.yaml, auth, billing, finance, or migrations.
tech_stack: GitHub pull request template in the app repo.
example: PR body links the Linear issue and leaves the risk box unchecked because infra/main.tf changed.
rules_and_restrictions: Product code and infra or workflow changes go in separate pull requests.
verifiers: CODEOWNERS requests the named owner when those paths change. Dobby asks to split a mixed PR. The template is a reminder, not a required form field.
agent_instructions: Split product code away from .github/workflows, infra/, and service.yaml.
automation: template/.github/pull_request_template.md.
v1_status: Template is in the repo.
discussion_point: Should a missing Linear link fail CI, or stay a reviewer habit?

what_we_do: The required check ci runs Ruff and the frontend typecheck and ESLint. Pytest runs when backend/tests contains test_*.py. The template ships with one health test.
tech_stack: GitHub Actions reusable workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml. Ruff. ESLint. TypeScript. pytest. Runs on a GitHub-hosted runner.
example: An old repo with no tests passes run_tests: false until the first test file exists. After that, pytest is required.
rules_and_restrictions: Lint always blocks the merge. Tests block the merge once a suite exists. The check name used by branch protection is ci / ci.
verifiers: Branch protection requires the check. A red check cannot merge.
agent_instructions: python.mdc: a behavior change lands with a test once the repo has a suite.
automation: App workflow calls opptra/sdlc/.github/workflows/ci.yml@v1.
v1_status: Workflow is in the repo. Template lint, test, and frontend build passed locally.
discussion_point: Is lint-only acceptable for the first month of migrating an old repo?

what_we_do: On the pull request, Terraform plans the target project and comments the add, change, and destroy list. A PR into staging plans opptra-staging. A PR into main plans prod_project. Nothing is built and nothing in GCP changes.
tech_stack: Terraform 1.10.5. Google provider. State in gs://<project>-tfstate/<app>. Workflow terraform-plan.yml. Module modules/cloud-run-service.
example: The comment shows one change: the Cloud Run image tag. Or it shows a destroy because someone removed the service from infra/.
rules_and_restrictions: Terraform is the only way to create, change, or delete app resources. gcloud run deploy is not used. The plan on the PR is what a person reads. Apply uses a fresh plan for the commit that actually merged, because the merge SHA can differ.
verifiers: Required check plan / plan. The reviewer looks at the comment before approving. A plan that errors fails the check.
agent_instructions: Change GCP only by editing infra/ or the shared module. Read the plan comment. Dobby treats an unexpected destroy as blocking.
automation: template/.github/workflows/plan.yml calls terraform-plan.yml.
v1_status: Workflow and module are in the repo. Validated locally. Not run against GCP.
discussion_point: deletion_protection on Cloud Run is false, so a destroy in the plan will really delete the service on apply. Do we want a two-step delete instead?

what_we_do: Dobby posts a short brief before a person is pinged: what changed, risk, whether CI is green, at most three files to open, blocking items, and nits. One human approval merges. Dobby does not count as that approval.
tech_stack: Dobby, the existing review app. Spec is dobby/review-brief.md. GitHub branch protection requires one approval.
example: Brief says risk needs a human because infra/ changed, CI is green, and there is nothing blocking. A person approves.
rules_and_restrictions: Blocking findings request changes. Nits do not. The human is pinged again only when a new commit adds a blocking finding or changes the risk. A Dobby finding becomes a required check only after we trust that class of comment.
verifiers: Branch protection requires one human approval and dismisses stale reviews. Dobby is a comment, not a required check, in v1.
agent_instructions: dobby/review-brief.md. Needs a human for workflows, infra, service.yaml, auth, billing, finance, migrations, secrets, and any destroy.
automation: Dobby already runs. It does not yet post this brief. That change is in the Dobby repo, after this spec is agreed.
v1_status: Spec is in the repo. Dobby behavior is not updated.
discussion_point: Agree the brief text before changing Dobby. Who is the human approver for apps that have a single owner?

what_we_do: CODEOWNERS requests the named owner, in addition to the one human approval, when the diff touches workflows, service.yaml, infra, auth, billing, finance, or migrations.
tech_stack: GitHub CODEOWNERS. Placeholder team @opptra/platform.
example: A PR that only changes a React page needs one approval. A PR that edits infra/main.tf also needs the platform owner.
rules_and_restrictions: The placeholder team must be replaced with a real team or with usernames before code-owner review is enabled. A missing team blocks every merge.
verifiers: GitHub code-owner review, once enabled. It is not turned on by protect-branches.sh today. That script requires one approval, not code owners.
agent_instructions: Dobby flags these paths as needs a human. The agent is told to split them out of product PRs.
automation: CODEOWNERS file. Enabling the requirement is a follow-up on the branch protection rule.
v1_status: File is in the template. The enforcement switch is not on.
discussion_point: Who is @opptra/platform in real GitHub usernames, and do we turn on code-owner review for the pilot?

step: Build the image and apply on merge to staging
what_we_do: A GitHub-hosted runner builds the image, tags it with the merge commit, pushes it to Artifact Registry in opptra-staging, plans again, and applies. Apply creates or updates the runtime service account, the Cloud Run service, and invoker IAM. It deletes a resource only when infra/ no longer contains it.
tech_stack: GitHub Actions deploy-cloud-run.yml. Docker. Artifact Registry apps in asia-south1. Terraform apply. Cloud Run, 1 CPU, 512Mi, min instances 0, port 8080.
example: Merge of abc123 to staging pushes asia-south1-docker.pkg.dev/opptra-staging/apps/gcc-dashboard:abc123 and applies it.
rules_and_restrictions: No laptop deploy. No second click in a GitHub Environment. The pull request approval is the gate. auth app-login and public grant allUsers invoker. auth iap turns on Identity-Aware Proxy and does not grant allUsers.
verifiers: The job curls /api/health and fails if it is not 200, except for iap. It comments the staging URL on the pull request. Concurrency locks one apply per app per environment.
agent_instructions: Do not add a parallel deploy path. The workflow is the release.
automation: template/.github/workflows/deploy.yml on push to staging calls deploy-cloud-run.yml.
v1_status: Workflow is in the repo. It has not deployed anything.
discussion_point: allUsers will fail if the org policy blocks public invokers. Do internal apps use iap by default instead?

what_we_do: The person who opens the promotion pull request opens the staging URL and reads the production plan comment.
tech_stack: The staging Cloud Run URL commented by the workflow. The pull request template has a checkbox for this.
example: Open https://gcc-dashboard-....run.app, click through the filter, then open the PR from staging to main and read the plan.
rules_and_restrictions: Production only receives commits that have been on staging. There is no browser test in v1.
verifiers: The checkbox is a reminder. A reviewer can block the promotion. Nothing automated checks that a person opened the URL.
agent_instructions: None. This is a human step.
automation: The URL comment only.
v1_status: Documented. Not enforced by a check.
discussion_point: Is a checkbox enough, or does the promotion PR need a named person to confirm staging?

what_we_do: A pull request from staging to main plans prod_project. The merge builds that commit and applies it in the prod project. Same workflow as staging. The branch chooses the project.
tech_stack: Same deploy-cloud-run.yml. State gs://<prod-project>-tfstate/<app>. GitHub environment name production, with no required reviewer.
example: Merge to main applies gcc-dashboard in opptra-datawarehouse, image tag equal to that merge commit.
rules_and_restrictions: No extra manual approve button after the pull request. No laptop gcloud. Image tag is the commit SHA, not latest.
verifiers: plan / plan on the promotion PR. ci / ci. One human approval. Health check after apply, except iap.
agent_instructions: Do not point a script at the prod project. prod_project comes from service.yaml.
automation: deploy.yml on push to main.
v1_status: Workflow is in the repo. Not run.
discussion_point: Some colleagues may want a second click for production. The current decision is that the pull request is the only approval.

what_we_do: Revert the commit on a branch off staging, merge to staging, then promote to main. The pipeline builds and applies the reverted commit.
tech_stack: git revert. The same plan and apply workflows. No separate redeploy-old-SHA button.
example: Revert abc123. Staging applies the revert. Then main applies it.
rules_and_restrictions: A rollback goes through staging. There is no workflow that redeploys an older tag directly to prod.
verifiers: The same checks as any other change. The plan shows the image tag moving back.
agent_instructions: AGENTS.md: rollback is a revert through staging, then main.
automation: The normal deploy workflow. No extra workflow.
v1_status: Rule only.
discussion_point: A revert through staging is slower than shifting Cloud Run traffic to the previous revision. Are we willing to accept that delay?

when_it_happens: After the app is in production
what_we_do: The template logger writes severity, message, service, and environment to stdout. Cloud Run ingests that stream.
tech_stack: Python logging in template/backend/app/logging.py. Cloud Run logs. No sidecar and no vendor.
example: A request failure shows up in Cloud Logging with severity ERROR and service gcc-dashboard.
rules_and_restrictions: Do not add a second logging library or a log shipper for a new app.
verifiers: Nothing in CI checks log shape. Review is the check.
agent_instructions: python.mdc: log JSON through the app logger.
automation: The logger is in the template. Cloud Run collects stdout without a workflow.
v1_status: In the template.
discussion_point: Is stdout JSON enough, or do we want a shared package and a required request id before more apps copy this?

when_it_happens: After the app is in production
what_we_do: After the first deploy, add three alerts per service to a Slack channel for that GCP project: 5xx above 1 percent for five minutes, no ready revision, and application ERROR logs.
tech_stack: Cloud Monitoring. Slack. docs/alerting.md. Not Terraform yet.
example: opptra-staging alerts go to the staging channel. opptra-datawarehouse alerts go to that project's channel.
rules_and_restrictions: One Slack channel per GCP project. A single failed probe should not page. iap services do not get a public uptime check in v1.
verifiers: No check fails the deploy if alerts are missing. The doc is the checklist a person follows.
agent_instructions: None in the agent rules yet.
automation: None. Creating the policies is manual.
v1_status: Written in docs/alerting.md. Not built.
discussion_point: The process sheet marks alerting as P0 and undecided. Do we block the pilot until these three alerts exist, or add them in the week after the first deploy?

when_it_happens: After the app is in production
what_we_do: frontend/src/analytics.ts is a no-op. A future PostHog trial lands in that file only.
tech_stack: None installed. PostHog is the candidate from the process sheet.
example: track() is called from a page later. Today it does nothing.
rules_and_restrictions: Do not add an analytics SDK in a new app until the trial is decided.
verifiers: react.mdc tells the agent to use that file. CI does not ban other SDKs.
agent_instructions: rules/cursor/react.mdc.
automation: None.
v1_status: Hook is in the template. No vendor.
discussion_point: Is PostHog the tool, and is usage instrumentation still P0 if the hook is empty?

when_it_happens: After the app is in production
what_we_do: A production bug or change request is a Linear issue on that app's project. The fix then follows the same branch, plan, staging, and main path.
tech_stack: Linear. No new ticketing tool.
example: Staging looked fine, prod filter is wrong. Open a Linear issue, branch off staging, promote as usual.
rules_and_restrictions: Do not hotfix prod from a laptop or from a branch that skipped staging.
verifiers: The same branch protection as any change.
agent_instructions: Start from the Linear issue.
automation: None.
v1_status: Process only.
discussion_point: One Linear project per app, or one project for all internal tools?

when_it_happens: When an old app is brought over
step: Add the contract before changing how it runs
what_we_do: Add service.yaml, infra/, the caller workflows, the agent rules, and render_tfvars.py. Point prod_project at the project that already runs production. Protect the branches. Get lint green. Leave the old deploy path in place until staging has applied once.
tech_stack: Same workflows. The old language can stay. docs/migrating.md lists five steps.
example: finance-ops keeps FastAPI, gains the workflows, and stops using a laptop script only after the GitHub apply has succeeded.
rules_and_restrictions: Do not combine the first GitHub production deploy with a move off a VM, off Vercel, or off a database on the same VM.
verifiers: The same CI and plan checks. The first plan should be an update after import, not a create.
agent_instructions: Do not delete deploy.sh until step 5 of migrating.md. Do not add a new framework while migrating.
automation: The app's new workflows. Import commands are in docs/resources.md and are run by a person once.
v1_status: Migration doc is written. No app has been migrated.
discussion_point: Pilot is finance-ops or github-mcp-server. Catalog, SCM, and the warehouse VM paths are the wrong first proof. Agree the pilot.

when_it_happens: When an old app is brought over
what_we_do: Before the first apply, import the existing Cloud Run service and runtime service account into that project's Terraform state. Then the plan updates them instead of creating a second copy.
tech_stack: terraform import. State prefix is the app name.
example: terraform import module.service.google_cloud_run_v2_service.app projects/opptra-applications/locations/asia-south1/services/finance-ops
rules_and_restrictions: Skip the import only when the service does not exist yet. A plan that says it will create a service which already exists is wrong and must not be applied.
verifiers: The person opening the first PR reads the plan. There is no automated import.
agent_instructions: Do not apply a plan that creates a duplicate of a live service.
automation: None. Commands are in docs/resources.md.
v1_status: Documented.
discussion_point: Who is allowed to run the import, since it needs permission the CI account may not have yet?

when_it_happens: When an app needs a database or a worker
step: Database and the shapes that are not built yet
what_we_do: Cloud SQL is added in the app's infra with prevent_destroy, so a plan cannot drop it until someone removes that block on purpose. A batch job must not start a backfill because an image changed. A VM runs only the worker. Apps Script uses clasp to staging, then clasp prod from main. A config repo has pull requests and lint and no deploy.
tech_stack: Cloud SQL Postgres 16 when needed. Cloud Run Jobs, MIG or VM, and Apps Script are later workflows. No module for them in v1.
example: opptra-scm-platform's Postgres moves to Cloud SQL. The app moves to Cloud Run. That is a later change, not part of the first pipeline migration.
rules_and_restrictions: Do not put Postgres on the app VM. Do not bake a production secret into an image. Shipping a job image does not run a backfill.
verifiers: No workflow enforces these yet. Review and the written docs are the check. Dobby flags a secret in the image.
agent_instructions: opptra-sdlc.mdc states the VM and database limits. The agent has no module to copy for a job or a VM.
automation: None for these shapes in v1.
v1_status: Written rules. No Terraform module and no workflow.
discussion_point: Which of these do we need in the second version: Cloud Run Jobs, the VM worker, or Apps Script?
